key_insight: A score-based reduced-order model can recover the stationary distribution of coarse turbulent flow variables and calibrate their dynamics to match observed finite-time statistics.
engineering_relevance: This offers a computationally cheap way to build accurate surrogate models for turbulent flows when full-resolution simulation or complete observations are unavailable.
method: Learn the stationary distribution of coarse variables from data using a score-based framework.
Construct a reduced-order stochastic model whose equilibrium distribution matches the learned data distribution by design.
Tune dynamics to reproduce finite-time correlations of shell-wise kinetic energies without forward model integration.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the model reproduces the stationary statistics of the resolved flow with high accuracy and is calibrated using finite-time energy correlations in individual wavenumber shells.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the training data captures the relevant turbulent regimes, and the approach may be sensitive to the choice of coarse variables and shell statistics.
paper_title: Score-based stochastic reduced-order models of barotropic quasi-geostrophic turbulence
